title: Penne Primavera with Spring Vegetables, Lemon and Parmesan
summary: Penne tossed with stir-fried spring vegetables, peas, butter, lemon and Parmesan for a light, bright pasta dish.
equipment: very large frying pan or sauté pan (32 cm) or a wide casserole

ingredients.item: fine salt for 4 litres of pasta water (0.8%)
ingredients.note: about 5.25 tsp; most of it goes down the drain

ingredients.item: asparagus, woody ends snapped off, cut into 3 cm pieces
red or yellow pepper, cut into strips (about 150 g)
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Boil the water
steps.text: Bring 4 litres of water to the boil with the 32 g salt, ready for the pasta.

steps.title: Stir-fry the vegetables
steps.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a very large frying pan over medium-high heat, add the broccoli and pepper and stir-fry for 3 minutes, then add the asparagus and courgette and cook for 3-4 minutes more, until everything looks bright and just tender with a little colour at the edges. Cooking the vegetables in stages like this, rather than all at once, is what keeps each one crisp-tender instead of stewed and soft.

steps.title: Add garlic and tomatoes
steps.text: Stir in the remaining oil, garlic and cherry tomatoes and cook for 1-2 minutes, just until the tomatoes begin to soften. Season, then take the pan off the heat.

steps.title: Cook the pasta and peas
steps.text: Cook the penne in the boiling water for 1 minute less than the packet time, adding the peas for the final 2 minutes. Reserve 240 ml of the cooking water, then drain.

steps.title: Combine and toss
steps.text: Add the pasta, peas, butter, lemon zest and 120 ml of the reserved water to the vegetables, and toss over medium heat for 1-2 minutes, until a light, glossy coating forms around everything. The starchy pasta water and melting butter are what bind the sauce together rather than leaving it watery.

steps.title: Finish off the heat
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and stir in the Parmesan and the lemon juice, tossing again until smooth. Adding the cheese and lemon juice only once the heat is off keeps the sauce silky instead of letting the cheese seize into clumps.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Scatter the torn basil over the top and serve straightaway, while the vegetables are still vivid and the pasta glossy.

tips: Cook the vegetables in stages rather than tipping them all in at once - the common mistake is crowding the pan, which steams everything into a uniform soft mush instead of keeping some bite.
Add the Parmesan and lemon juice only once the pan is off the heat, since direct heat can make the cheese clump instead of melting into the sauce.
Keep a close eye on the asparagus and courgette - a minute or two too long and they lose the bright colour and snap that make the dish feel fresh.
Reserve the pasta water before draining; it's easy to forget and the sauce depends on it to come together.
storage: Best eaten fresh, as the vegetables soften on standing, but leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a pan with a splash of water until piping hot, rather than in the microwave, to avoid the vegetables turning mushy. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
